bib.title: Codebook Agent: Amortized Topology Design for LLM Multi-Agent Systems

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "Codebook Agent: Amortized Topology Design for LLM Multi-Agent Systems", Jinxi Yu, Yubei Li, Eric Hanchen Jiang (equal contribution), Zhi Zhang, Dong Liu, Wenxiao Zhao, Levina Li, Kai-Wei Chang, Ying Nian Wu (UCLA). arXiv:2609.02264v1 [cs.AI], 2 Sep 2026. Preprint (AAAI-style format, no venue stated). Code: github.com/jinxiy1104/CodebookAgent.

COVERAGE: about 41,000 of 41,597 chars read, all body text and Tables 1-2. The last ~600 chars of the references (GraphRNN onward) were not displayed. The extraction is mostly clean, but spaces are missing in some paragraphs. There are no appendices.

CLAIMS (ranked)
1. The method is the most accurate on all six benchmarks.
- number: 84.62 average vs 83.02 for GTD (+1.60), 77.63 for Vanilla (+6.99)
- setup: gpt-4o-mini, temp 0.7, max tokens 1024. GSM8K, MATH, MultiArith, SVAMP, MBPP and HumanEval (Pass@1). 4-agent homogeneous teams. 9 learned-design baselines. Single run per configuration.
- quote: "Codebook Agent (ours) 94.8▲7.8 56.5▲8.9 99.4▲2.2 95.4▲6.9 83.5▲11.1 78.1▲5.0 84.62▲6.99"
- where: Table 1, p.5 (offset ~13k)
2. Edge count is negatively correlated with measured tokens, so edge-count cost surrogates are inverted.
- number: Pearson r ≈ -0.4
- setup: measured on the authors' own 300 execution records per benchmark
- quote: "edge count correlates with measured tokens atr≈ −0.4, because sparse communication yields longer completions, so minimizing|E|maximizesthe bill"
- where: Intro and Sec 4
- extra: the chain topology is the sparsest connected graph and "most token-expensive on every math-format benchmark".
3. Reward-surviving topologies collapse to about six distinct graphs, and a fixed topology is nearly as good as a generated one.
- number: about 6 codes used for every K≥8 (K from 4 to 64); the best fixed topology is within 1.4 accuracy points of every generated one
- setup: 7 settings. Accuracy moves ≤1.5 (GSM8K) or ≤2.5 (HumanEval) across K.
- quote: "the best fixed family (fully connected / chain / star) stays within 1.4accuracypointsofeverygeneratedtopologywemeasure"
- where: Q2 and Fig 5(b)
4. Which fixed graph wins depends on the setting.
- number: gaps up to 4.3 accuracy points and a 2.9x token factor (chain vs fully connected on MATH)
- quote: "fully connected on MATH, star on homogeneous HumanEval, chain on MMLU"
- where: Q2
5. A message-passing scorer cannot rank candidates when agents share a profile.
- number: none (an argument, not a measurement)
- setup: all x_i identical, so mean and sum aggregation give a pooled score independent of A
- quote: "whenx1 =· · ·=xN =x, any message-passing layer of Eq. (1) aggregates identical features over self-loops, so every node state—and thus the pooledscore—isindependentofA."
- where: Sec 4.3
- extra: the MLP proxy reading flattened adjacency was trained on measured utility and per-task normalized tokens (reward R = u - 0.1·τ̃, Eq. 2).
6. Reranker ablation: the MLP proxy gives the lowest token cost, ahead of random and the GNN.
- number: tokens per query on GSM8K / HumanEval-homo: MLP 927/546, random 1249/750, GNN 1711/918
- setup: same top-M=5 candidates, only the selector changes. Accuracy within 1.5 points.
- quote: "MLP927/546, random1249/750, GNN1711/918, with ac-curacy within1.5points—the ranking buys cost, not large Pass@1"
- where: Sec 5.3(c), Fig 5(c)
- extra: taking the predictor's top-1 costs 913 tokens on GSM8K, and reranking adds 0.6-1.0 accuracy points.
7. Design is much faster, and total tokens fall.
- number: 2.4 ms vs 301-396 ms (125-158x); tokens down 21.9-33.2% vs the iterative decoder + edge-count GNN pipeline
- examples: 1239→927 (GSM8K), 2304→1611 (MATH), 624→417 (HumanEval-het); MATH wall clock 43.7→27.4 min
- quote: "mean tokens drop 21.9–33.2%(e.g.1239→927GSM8K,2304→1611MATH,699→546HumanEval-homo,624→417HumanEval-het)"
- where: Q4
8. The ranking transfers to another backbone.
- number: Qwen-3-8B average 74.0 vs GTD 72.7 and G-Designer 72.1
- setup: GSM8K, MATH and MMLU (3 experts). Scores 92.7/63.5/65.8; CoT average 67.5.
- quote: "Codebook Agent still leads every column (92.7/63.5/65.8, avg.74.0) over GTD (72.7) andG-Designer(72.1)"
- where: Table 2
9. The method also scales with team size, which suggests topology selection stays useful as teams grow.
- number: HumanEval rises 71.9→87.5 for N=2..10; GSM8K is flat at 93.0-95.5
- quote: "HumanEval rises71.9→87.5"
- where: Fig 5(a)
10. Cost weight: λ = -0.1 is the chosen operating point.
- number: λ=0 costs 1108/743 tokens (GSM8K/HumanEval) with no accuracy gain; at -0.4 tokens fall to 927/442; accuracy peaks at -0.1/-0.2
- where: Fig 5(d)

METHOD (for the note)
- Offline: 50 training tasks per benchmark, each run under 6 fixed topologies (complete, chain, star, 3 Erdős–Rényi), giving 300 records.
- A VQ autoencoder (K=16 codes, dz=32) is trained only on successful topologies (u>0.5).
- An MLP predicts a distribution over codes from the query embedding (all-MiniLM-L6-v2, d=384). Targets are reward-weighted with γ=2.
- At test time the top M=5 codes are decoded and deduplicated. One batched MLP proxy call picks argmax(û - λĉ). There are no LLM calls and no message passing in design.

LIMITS
- Single evaluation run per configuration, with no variance or seeds reported.
- The design-axis ablations use 200 tasks per benchmark.
- Six of the seven design-axis settings use homogeneous teams. Only HumanEval has a heterogeneous 4-role team, where the incumbent is slightly more accurate (78.8 vs 78.1).
- The GNN-is-blind result is specific to identical profiles.
- The authors say the incumbent-scorer token numbers are "not comparable to the full incumbentpipeline".
- Only gpt-4o-mini and Qwen-3-8B, with small teams (N=3-4 in the main results). Tasks are math, code and MMLU, not open-ended agentic work.
- The codebook is trained per benchmark on 300 records, so it needs real LLM runs for each new setting.
- Fixed topologies come within 1.4 points of the generated ones, so the accuracy headroom from topology design is small.
- The r≈-0.4 correlation is measured on the authors' own records. The causal explanation (sparse communication gives longer completions) is stated, not tested.
- Baseline numbers appear to be rerun by the authors under their own protocol. This is not stated explicitly.

BUILDS ON
- VQ-VAE (van den Oord, Vinyals, Kavukcuoglu, NeurIPS 2017); VQ-VAE-2 (Razavi et al., NeurIPS 2019).
- VQGraph (Yang et al., ICLR 2024), for the structure-token regularizer.
- G-Designer (Zhang et al. 2025c) variational designer; ARG-Designer (Li et al., AAAI 2026) autoregressive; GTD (Jiang et al., ACL 2026) graph diffusion; TopoDIM (Sun et al., Findings of ACL 2026).
- GPTSwarm (Zhuge et al. 2024); AgentDropout (Wang et al., ACL 2025); DyLAN (Liu et al., COLM 2024); MaAS; AFLOW (Zhang et al. 2025d); ADAS (Hu, Lu, Clune, ICLR 2025).
- Cost and failure context: "Are More LLM Calls All You Need?" (Chen et al., NeurIPS 2024); "Why Do Multi-Agent LLM Systems Fail?" (Cemri et al., NeurIPS 2025 D&B).
- GAT (Veličković et al., ICLR 2018) is used as the GNN scorer.

CODE: none printed in the paper. Key equations are Eq. 2 (reward), Eq. 6 (soft targets) and Eq. 11: A*(c)=argmax_{A in A(c)}(û(A,c)-λĉ(A,c)).

FIGURES (one candidate)
- Fig 1, p.1: "Three regimes of topology design." It contrasts fixed topology, an iterative query-conditioned generator, and a codebook with a single proxy call. It is the fastest way to see the contrast with the generate-and-score recipe.
- Alternative: Fig 3 (accuracy vs latency Pareto on MATH).

PROBLEMS: Extraction is missing spaces in places. The figure text is jumbled, and the Fig 5 panels are described only through their captions and body text. No embedded instructions were found. The arXiv ID 2609.02264 and the date, Sep 2026, are as printed on the PDF. Several cited works are also 2026 papers.
